news_drafts.headline: Blaenau Gwent draws £1.4m from reserves to cover spending overspend
news_drafts.lead: Blaenau Gwent dipped into its financial reserves during 2025/26 to cover an overall overspend against budget. The council drew £1.4m from its Financial Planning and Resilience reserves to fund an adverse variance, while specific reserves fell by a net £1.964m overall and school balances were reduced by £2.051m. Against this, the council's capital programme delivered at 86.2%, spending £41.1m of a £47.7m budget, with £6.5m of work carried forward into 2026/27. Four capital schemes recorded combined overspends of £80k, but these were accommodated within available resources. The council also secured £6.3m in new external funding for regeneration schemes in the final quarter, including £2.31m for Ebbw Vale Multi Storey car park refurbishment and £1.85m for Old Abertillery Library.

findings.headline: Council has not made sufficient progress addressing outstanding recommendations on corporate safeguarding, with progress described as too slow.
findings.detail: Follow-up review of corporate safeguarding arrangements found insufficient progress on implementing previous audit recommendations. While some recent activity to strengthen arrangements had occurred, the auditor noted progress was too slow and limited opportunities existed for members to scrutinise and challenge the timeliness of progress.
findings.matters: Slow progress on safeguarding arrangements exposes the council and vulnerable service users to risk and indicates weak implementation capability.
findings.quote: I found that the Council had not made sufficient progress to fully address the outstanding recommendations. While there had been some recent activity to strengthen arrangements, progress had been too slow with limited opportunities for members to scrutinise and challenge the timeliness of progress.

findings.headline: Procurement rules not followed, identified as a significant audit issue.
findings.detail: One of two significant issues reported in the audit findings relates to failure to follow procurement rules. The audit team made a recommendation for the Council to ensure it follows its own procurement procedures in future.
findings.matters: Procurement control failures indicate weaker governance and expose the council to financial loss, reputational damage, and potential legal challenge.
findings.quote: We reported two significant issues in relation to procurement rules not being adhered to, and the quality and timeliness of the accounts.

findings.headline: One uncorrected material misstatement: five fixed assets over-depreciated by £1.25 million due to incorrect Useful Economic Life.
findings.detail: The audit identified an uncorrected misstatement above the reporting level where five fixed assets had their Useful Economic Life recorded incorrectly, resulting in over-depreciation of £1.25 million. The council did not correct this error before the accounts were signed.
findings.matters: A material uncorrected misstatement affects the reliability of the balance sheet and asset valuations reported to members, officers, and creditors.
findings.quote: There was one uncorrected misstatement, relating to ﬁve ﬁxed assets where the Useful Economic Life was incorrect, and resulted in these assets being over depreciated by £1.25 million.

findings.headline: Accounts submitted 8 months after the statutory deadline of 31 October 2025, with audit opinion issued 2 July 2026.
findings.detail: The draft financial statement was received on 8 February 2026, well beyond the Welsh Government deadline. The audit opinion was issued on 2 July 2026, 8 months after the statutory deadline. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion despite the delay.
findings.matters: Late accounts submission indicates governance or operational capacity issues and affects the council's ability to respond to financial pressures in real time.
findings.figures: 8 months late; statutory deadline 31 October 2025; accounts received 8 February 2026; opinion issued 2 July 2026
findings.quote: The draft accounts were presented for audit on 8 February 2026. This was 8 months after the deadline of 31 October 2025 set by the Welsh Government.

findings.headline: Authority has introduced an audit report tracker and refined the corporate governance framework, with establishment of new governance and risk management groups.
findings.detail: The Committee welcomed additional measures introduced during the period, including an audit report tracker to log and monitor recommendations arising from concerns and audit reports to ensure robust implementation or escalation where needed. The authority also refined its Corporate Governance Framework and established the Governance, Risk, Integrity, Performance and Partnership Group and Corporate Risk Management Group to improve organisational oversight and effective risk management.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender would see these measures as strengthening the council's control environment and capacity to track audit recommendations, supporting governance confidence.
findings.quote: The introduction of an audit report tracker to log and monitor all recommendations arising from concerns and audit reports will ensure that they are robustly implemented and/or escalated in the event of non compliance or barriers to completion.
